In [[epidemiology]], '''preventable fraction among the unexposed''' (PF<small>u</small>) is the proportion of incidents in the unexposed group that could be prevented by exposure. It is calculated as <math>PF_u = (I_u - I_e)/I_u = 1 - RR</math>, where <math>I_e</math> is the [[incidence (epidemiology)|incidence]] in the exposed group, <math>I_u</math> is the incidence in the unexposed group, and <math>RR</math> is the [[relative risk]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Essentials of epidemiology in public health|last=Aschengrau|first=Ann|last2=Seage|first2=George R.|date=2014|publisher=Jones & Bartlett Learning|isbn=9781449657338|edition=3rd|location=Burlington, MA|pages=67|oclc=826123155}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Modern epidemiology|last=Rothman|first=Kenneth J.|last2=Greenland|first2=Sander|last3=Lash|first3=Timothy L.|publisher=Lippincott Williams & Wilkins|year=2012|isbn=9780781755641|edition=3rd|location=Philadelphia|oclc=169455558}}</ref> It is a synonym of the [[relative risk reduction]].

It is used when an exposure reduces the risk, as opposed to increasing it, in which case its symmetrical notion is [[attributable fraction among the exposed]].{{cn|date=May 2023}}
